clue.text: By river, assist old boy to return to the country

parts.note: the Cam is the river that flows through Cambridge

indicators.note: to return asks for the two pieces assist and old boy to be read together backwards

parts.note: to assist is to aid
OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Someone down by a river is told to help a former pupil get back home to his native land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses assist and old boy together as one run, giving BODIA; 'the country' is the definition, not a rural setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a nation of South-East Asia, so it is a country.

clue.text: Firm measure taken gains only valueless foreign money

parts.note: CO, short for company, is the usual crossword firm
a peck is an old dry measure of volume, a quarter of a bushel

explanation.surface: A company takes some action but ends up earning only worthless overseas currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle words 'taken gains only' are surface padding linking the charade to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This coin was a hundredth of a Russian rouble, an almost worthless piece of foreign coinage.

clue.text: Kill a lot of crows

explanation.definitionFit: To kill someone unlawfully is homicide, and the collective noun for a flock of crows is the same word.

clue.text: Sophie has a go, replacing inner tubes

indicators.note: replacing tells us the letters of the name and the phrase are put back in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Sophie tries her hand at fitting new inner tubes to a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' rearranges SOPHIE + AGO. 'inner tubes' suggests tyres, but means body passages: the gullets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gullets are the food pipes inside the body, literally internal tubes, and the word here is the Latin plural.

clue.text: While travelling, knowledge is retained of the immovable

indicators.note: is retained means the knowledge is held inside the travelling phrase

parts.note: something on the move is in transit
gen is British slang for information or knowledge

explanation.surface: Information is kept on journeys, the clue says, about something that cannot be shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN sits inside IN TRANSIT, between its I and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uncompromising refuses to budge, so they are immovable.

clue.text: Take his works from the library

definitions.text: Take his works from the library

parts.words: Take his works from the library
parts.note: reads as advice to fetch an author's books from a lending library, the verb for doing that also being the surname of the Victorian writer of Lavengro

explanation.surface: Advice to fetch a particular author's books from the library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his works' points to George Borrow, the nineteenth-century English travel writer; taking any book from a library is the same verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a library book out on loan is the everyday verb, and the same word is the writer's surname.

clue.text: Love game, it turns out, in the end

parts.note: love means nil in tennis scoring, written as the round letter O

indicators.note: it turns out signals that the letters of the word game turn into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A love match, as things happen, finishes well at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love game' reads as a tennis match, but love is just the letter O; 'it turns out' rearranges the game into MEGA, and 'the end' is the Greek alphabet's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the finish, as in alpha and omega.

clue.text: Course of duty can start generating revolutionary movement

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of turns of duty
a tin is a can

indicators.note: start points to the opening letter of the word generating

explanation.surface: A duty roster may set off a political uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary movement' sounds political but means spinning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning on an axis is literally moving in revolutions, so the gerund names circular motion.

clue.text: Guard in armour?

explanation.walkthrough: Split as WAR DRESS, the word is what a soldier wears for battle; the question mark flags that whimsical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A female prison officer is a guard, and clothing for battle, read as two words, describes armour.

clue.text: Relies on host to survive — parties a problem!

indicators.note: problem suggests the letters of parties and a are in trouble and need sorting out into new order

explanation.surface: A party-giver depends on a host to get by, but parties bring trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges PARTIES + A. The definition is descriptive: an organism that depends on a host.
explanation.definitionFit: Such an organism lives on or in another creature and feeds from it, unable to survive alone.

clue.text: Old man with a cosy home gold provided

parts.note: a nest is a snug home
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An elderly man has a snug house, provided there is money.
explanation.walkthrough: Nestor was the aged, wise king in Homer's Iliad, so his name stands for any wise old man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Homeric king's name is used for a wise elder or senior figure.

clue.text: A conker's a nut — can be prickly, too!

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters of the phrase could be made into something else

explanation.surface: Someone grumpily insists a conker is a nut, and a spiky one at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges ACONKERSANUT. A conker is a horse-chestnut seed in a spiky case, used in a British children's game.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad-tempered, quarrelsome person is irritable and touchy, or prickly.

clue.text: Look back at century and grovel

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: back shows the word for look is read in reverse

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: Someone glances back at a hundred years and then fawns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for look, giving REEP, which the century letter is placed before despite the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: To act obsequiously, fawning on superiors, is to crawl or grovel.

clue.text: Are basalt rocks statuary material?

indicators.note: rocks is a verb here, shaking the letters of are and basalt into a new order

explanation.surface: Is basalt the right rock for carving statues?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like geology, but it shakes ARE + BASALT into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: This fine white stone, a form of gypsum, is carved into statues and ornaments.

clue.text: Taking advantage, leading huntsman jumps over the dogs

indicators.note: taking means the word for jumps takes in, or holds, the other pieces

parts.note: bounds are leaps or jumps
an asset is a benefit or advantage

indicators.note: leading points to the opening letter of the word huntsman

explanation.surface: A hunt master, seizing his chance, leaps over the hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' means BOUNDS takes in the other pieces; 'leading huntsman' is just its first letter H, not a master of hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: These are short-legged hunting hounds with long ears, so they are a breed of dog.

clue.text: Concerned with smell? Look up to the plant

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word for look is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
a plant is an industrial works, a factory

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs and glances up toward the industrial plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LO into OL. 'plant' suggests a flower one might smell, but means works.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything relating to the sense of smell, such as the nerves of the nose.

clue.text: Fellow's a rotter, torturing mice

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter

indicators.note: torturing means the letters of mice are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A college fellow turns out to be a cruel cad who torments mice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torturing' rearranges MICE into EMIC. 'Fellow' means a college don, not just a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A university fellow is a scholar or don, a member of a college's teaching staff.

clue.text: They are chirpy although cold and with childish malnutrition evident

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
rickets is a bone disease of children caused by lack of vitamin D

explanation.surface: Children are cheerful though cold and visibly underfed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chirpy' looks like 'cheerful' but means literally chirping.
explanation.definitionFit: These insects make a chirping sound by rubbing their wings, so they are literally chirpy.

clue.text: Detailing equipment used by farmer's wife

definitions.text: Detailing equipment used by farmer's wife

parts.words: Detailing equipment used by farmer's wife
parts.note: detailing is read as de-tailing, cutting off tails, which the farmer's wife did to three blind mice in the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: Tools for fine handiwork belonging to a farmer's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Three Blind Mice, the farmer's wife cuts off their tails with a kitchen blade; 'detailing' looks like fine work.
explanation.definitionFit: A large kitchen blade for slicing joints of meat is what the rhyme says she used.

clue.text: Place old prophet on Ganges boat

parts.note: to place is to put
Eli was the priest and prophet who raised Samuel in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone sets an ancient prophet aboard a vessel on India's holy river.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an obscure Indian word, so the wordplay carries it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a flat-bottomed sailing vessel used on the Ganges river in India.

clue.text: Moving in on us, by agreement

indicators.note: moving shows that the letters of in on us shift around into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone advances on us, by mutual consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges IN ON US.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting together in complete harmony or concord is a state of agreement.

clue.text: Progressive decline of French musical beat

parts.note: de is French for of
a cadence is a rhythm, or a closing sequence of chords in music

explanation.surface: A gradual fall-off in French musical rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral or cultural deterioration over time is a steady decline.

clue.text: Live with daughter in fine fettle

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
someone in fine fettle is healthy, or well

explanation.surface: Someone lives with their daughter and is in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside or inhabit a place is to live there.

clue.text: Check tea-dispenser — it should have milk in it

definitions.text: it should have milk in it

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
an urn is a large vessel for dispensing tea

explanation.surface: Inspect the tea urn: it ought to contain milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it should have milk in it' sounds like tea but describes a dairy vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A large metal can for carrying or making butter from dairy produce holds milk.

clue.text: Even more like a lamb

parts.note: lambs are proverbially gentle and submissive, so this asks for the comparative of that quality

explanation.surface: Someone becomes still more lamb-like.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'as gentle as a lamb' gives the quality; 'even more' asks for its comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambs symbolise humble mildness, so being more lamb-like is being more submissive.

clue.text: Military personnel we hear may be shelled

indicators.note: we hear means a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: kernels are the seeds or nuts inside shells

explanation.surface: Army officers, it is said, may come under shellfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be shelled' looks military but means husked: KERNELS sounds like the officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior army officers ranking above majors are military people.

clue.text: A rook on board

parts.note: rook here is the chess piece, standing on a chessboard, not the bird

explanation.surface: A crow perches on a plank.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird reading is the false path; in chess the rook has another common name.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the rook, which moves in straight lines, is also called a fortress piece.

clue.text: Donkey at rainy resort for a race

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, so the letters of rainy are sorted again

explanation.surface: A donkey at a wet seaside town is entered for a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a seaside town but means re-sort, rearranging RAINY into YRIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient people of Mesopotamia formed a distinct nation or ethnic group.
